reason: E1 supports MoO2 formation and the specific friction/wear reductions in a nitride coating, but the hypothesis extrapolates this to a bulk HEA without evidence for similar Mo segregation, oxidation kinetics, or film stability. E2 and E3 provide only general background on friction and a different self-lubricating HEA system, respectively, offering no direct support for the key premises.
premises: Mo addition can reduce friction coefficient and wear rate by forming a MoO2 lubricating layer
The MoO2 layer forms in-situ during sliding due to frictional heat and oxidation
A friction coefficient reduction of ~50% and wear rate reduction by an order of magnitude are achievable
These tribological improvements are effective across a wide temperature range (RT to ~600°C)
The mechanism is transferable from (AlCrTiZrMox)N coatings to a bulk CoCrFeMnNi HEA
